clue.text: Talk Talk's lawyers flipped coin

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the word for the legal profession is read from right to left

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
a bit is an old small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: The band Talk Talk's legal team toss a coin to settle something.
explanation.walkthrough: Talk Talk was a British band, which disguises the definition. To rabbit, or rabbit on, is British slang for chattering at length.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit means to chatter or go on at length, so it can stand for talk.

clue.text: Improving the flavour of an egg I scrambled

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are mixed up, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook claims scrambling an egg makes it taste better.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese, wine and meat are left to mature over time precisely so that their taste develops and improves.

clue.text: Light touches single part of painting

parts.note: a brush is a light touch in passing
a stroke is a gentle caressing touch

explanation.surface: An artist's delicate dabs make up just one section of a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'touches' supplies two light touches, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Each mark made by one movement of the artist's brush is a single component of the finished picture.

clue.text: It's very unlikely that, ultimately, everything's blue

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: last letter of the word
everything is all
taken as written
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, whose members are Tories

explanation.surface: A doubter says it is hard to believe that everything has turned out sad.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, whose members are called Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, scarcely credible account is called a tall story, so it is something very improbable.

clue.text: Shoe company's third chance, missing second round

indicators.note: the third of a word is its third letter, so only that one is taken from the business word

parts.note: third letter of the word

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the named round letter is dropped from the result

parts.note: an occasion is an opportunity or chance
a round letter is O; it is the second O that goes

explanation.surface: A footwear firm gets one more try after failing in the second round of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoe company' reads as a firm, but 'company' only lends its third letter. Of the two O's, the second one is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather slip-on, originally Native American footwear, so it is a type of shoe.

clue.text: Play item Bach arranged without second violin part

indicators.note: music that is arranged is rewritten, so the letters are set in a new order
without means lacking, so that selected letter is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: second picks out just the letter in position two of the instrument's name

parts.note: second letter of the word violin; part says only a piece of it is meant

explanation.surface: A musician plays a Bach piece arranged to leave out the second violin's part.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is one of Shakespeare's tragedies, so it is an example of a stage play.

clue.text: Tea-room entrance

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea
RM is the standard abbreviation of room

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway noun; it is the verb meaning to delight. Cha (or char) is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to delight or captivate them, which is what entrance means as a verb.

clue.text: Undress hirsute character

indicators.note: to undress is to strip off the outer layers, so the outside letters of the word are removed

parts.note: hirsute means covered in hair

explanation.surface: An instruction to a hairy person to take their clothes off.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is the manner or impression a person gives, so it means their character or bearing.

clue.text: Without a bit of evidence, assume an archaeological site's beneath you

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the selected letter is dropped from the verb

parts.note: to infer is to conclude or suppose

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
a is the indefinite article, like an
a dig is an excavation site

explanation.surface: A scornful archaeologist says guessing about a site without proof is unworthy of a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: Infra dig is short for the Latin infra dignitatem, below one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infra dig is considered beneath one's dignity, which is what 'beneath you' says idiomatically.

clue.text: Country club I rebuilt next to theatre

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A country club is reconstructed beside the local playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state without a monarch, so it is one kind of nation or country.

clue.text: Cut off ends of airtight bag doctor provided

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside, so those outer letters enclose the rest
the ends of a word are its first and last letters, with the middle discarded

parts.note: outer letters of the word
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A doctor trims the ends off a sealed bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airtight bag' looks like a single object, but 'bag' is the verb that wraps the outer letters round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adrift is cut off and drifting, isolated without moorings or connection.

clue.text: One section of popular board game's missing edges

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one of the named letters is dropped from the game

parts.note: chess is played on a board
s. abbreviates section; only one of the pair is removed

explanation.surface: Part of a well-liked board game has lost its borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges' reads as the board's borders; it is the verb meaning moves gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move slowly by small amounts, just as someone edges along.

clue.text: Space in the brain for milky solid

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
mental means in the mind

explanation.surface: Making room in one's head for some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Em is a printing term for a space as wide as the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese, and cheese is a solid made from curdled milk.

clue.text: Don't princes set out to be dull?

indicators.note: to set out is to lay things out afresh, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A question asking whether royal sons set out to be boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nondescript lacks distinctive features, so it is plain, uninteresting and unremarkable.

clue.text: Furiously sound horn to pass lowcoach

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn
to hand is to pass
a slowcoach is a snail, and the clue's word lacks its opening letter

explanation.surface: An impatient driver hoots angrily to get past a dawdling coach.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'lowcoach' is slowcoach with its first letter gone, so the snail it means loses its first letter too; there is no separate deletion word. A slowcoach is a slow person.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight tooth and nail is to fight with every resource, fiercely and with great vigour.

clue.text: As part of revolting chores, I lube nurse's medical equipment

indicators.note: revolting is read as turning over, so the run of letters is taken backwards
as part of means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of chores, I, lube and the start of nurse

explanation.surface: A hospital worker grumbles about having to oil a nurse's kit among other horrible jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuliser turns liquid medicine into a fine mist for inhaling, a piece of medical apparatus.

clue.text: Mock man that exaggerates his manhood

parts.note: cod means mock or sham, as in cod philosophy
a man in chess or draughts is a piece

explanation.surface: A jibe at a man who boasts about his masculinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock man' reads as ridiculing someone; cod is the British adjective for fake, and a man is a playing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a pouch on Renaissance breeches that drew attention to, and padded out, the male genitals.

clue.text: Adapt — no; lob, mall — yes

indicators.note: to adapt is to alter and refashion, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A verdict on words: one is rejected, two others accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue sorts words: 'adapt' has two syllables, so no, while 'lob' and 'mall' each have one, so yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A word spoken in a single syllable, such as lob or mall, is a monosyllable by definition.

clue.text: Understand butcher can't haggle over lambs' heads

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so the letters are chopped and reordered

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: heads are what come first, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: first letters of the words

explanation.surface: A meat trader refuses to bargain over the price of sheep's heads.
explanation.definitionFit: To latch on is informal for finally grasping an idea, so it means to understand.

clue.text: Silver lining nothing but miserable

indicators.note: a lining sits inside something, so the metal goes within the following phrase

parts.note: mere means nothing more than
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A pessimist says every silver lining is just wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver lining' looks like the idiom for hope; here silver lines the inside of another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable can mean pitifully small or inadequate, as a miserable sum, which is what meagre means.

clue.text: Profiting from every version of film shot with gloves on?

parts.note: to be up is to be in profit
per means for each
a cut is an edited version of a film, as in director's cut

explanation.surface: Someone cashes in on each edit of a film scene shot while wearing gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a film take; it is a blow, and the gloves are boxing gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch thrown upward in boxing, a blow delivered by a gloved fist.

clue.text: Top businessman pockets two pounds in giant fiddle

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so the executive wraps round the money

parts.note: a chief executive officer is the top person in a business
L is the abbreviation for pound, twice

explanation.surface: A company boss takes a couple of pounds as part of a huge fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a swindle, which fits the dodgy boss; it is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large member of the violin family, and a fiddle is an informal word for a violin.

clue.text: Cold, enjoyed outside, as an ice-lolly should be

indicators.note: outside means placed round the edge, so the verb surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: liked means enjoyed
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An ice-lolly is best cold and enjoyed outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enjoyed outside' suggests eating in the open air; it means enjoyed goes round the letter for cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-lolly is a frozen treat on a stick that is eaten by licking it.

clue.text: Small nasty unfinished bit of protein in cereal?

indicators.note: unfinished means without its end, so the last letter of the adjective is cut

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
vile means nasty

explanation.surface: A disgusted eater finds a small, unpleasant half-formed piece of protein in their breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a jokey definition: a beetle in your cereal adds unwanted protein.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle that infests stored grain, so finding one in breakfast cereal is extra protein.

clue.text: Box up electronic parts for medical professional

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
something that parts splits open, letting another letter go between

parts.note: the box is British slang for television
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Instructions to pack up electronic components for a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is British slang for the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A vet is a veterinary surgeon, a qualified practitioner who gives medical treatment to animals.

clue.text: Enjoys going round smart seaside resort

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the verb wraps round the word for hurt

parts.note: to have is to enjoy, as in enjoy good health
to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: Someone likes touring a stylish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective for the resort; it is the verb meaning to hurt. Hastings is a town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is a town on the East Sussex coast that is a traditional English holiday destination by the sea.

clue.text: Audible smell fellow inhales wife expelled

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word for odour is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: a scent is a smell

indicators.note: to inhale is to take in, so the man's word draws the spouse letter inside

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A college fellow sniffs a smell as his wife is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college, the very place a student is sent down from.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who is sent down is expelled from a British university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: Cad objectified woman? Quite

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel
her is the object form of she

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a bounder treated a woman as an object, answered with a guarded agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectified' sounds like sexism; it means the grammatical object case, so she becomes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather and quite are both adverbs of degree meaning to a fair extent, fairly or somewhat.
